parts.content_target: Separate and interpret hydrolysis products by chromatography, then plan an extraction/separation method. Plan an investigation with predictions, suitable apparatus and techniques.
parts.credit_requirement: Plan chromatography of hydrolysed food extract: prepare/filter sample (1), pencil baseline above solvent (1), small dried sample/reference spots (1), develop in covered chamber (1), mark solvent front and visualise spots appropriately (1), compare with references for a conclusion (1).
parts.prompt: Plan chromatography to compare the components of a teacher-prepared carbohydrate hydrolysate with glucose and reference sugar B. Include preparation, apparatus, development, observation and a defensible conclusion. No specific locating-agent identity is required.
parts.canonical_answer: Filter a suitable diluted portion of the teacher-prepared hydrolysate if suspended solids remain. Draw a pencil baseline above a shallow solvent reservoir in a covered chamber. Apply small hydrolysate, glucose and B spots in separate lanes, drying between applications. Develop all lanes on the same paper in the same solvent, with the paper upright and solvent initially below the baseline. Remove the paper before the front reaches the top, mark the solvent front immediately, and visualise the spots by a suitable supervised method. Compare positions or Rf values with references: in the chromatography example the two detected sample spots match glucose and B, supporting their possible presence rather than proving unique identities.
marking_guidance: Prepare an appropriate sample, including filtration if needed (1).
Pencil baseline above solvent with suitable chamber/paper arrangement (1).
Small dried sample and reference spots in separate lanes (1).
Develop together in covered chamber under the same solvent conditions (1).
Mark front promptly and visualise spots suitably (1).
Compare reference positions/Rf for a qualified conclusion (1). Accept equivalent sound sequencing; no named locating chemical required.
